record.original_question: Is the Kobayashi metric complete on a bounded smooth pseudoconvex domain?

evidence.quote: Problem 7.5.1 Is k complete on a bounded smooth pseudoconvex domain?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^n$ be a bounded domain with smooth boundary that is pseudoconvex (i.e., $\Omega$ admits a smooth plurisubharmonic exhaustion function, or equivalently, the boundary $\partial\Omega$ is Levi pseudoconvex). For points $p, q \in \Omega$, define the Kobayashi pseudodistance $k_\Omega(p,q)$ as the infimum of sums $\sum_{i=1}^N \rho(z_i, w_i)$, where $\rho$ is the Poincaré distance on the unit disk $\mathbb{D} \subset \mathbb{C}$, taken over all finite chains of holomorphic disks $f_i : \mathbb{D} \to \Omega$ with $f_i(z_i) = p_{i-1}$, $f_i(w_i) = p_i$, $p_0 = p$, $p_N = q$. 

Question: Is $(\Omega, k_\Omega)$ always a complete metric space for every bounded smooth pseudoconvex domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^n$?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of whether every bounded smooth pseudoconvex domain in $\mathbb{C}^n$ is Kobayashi complete remains a well-known open problem in several complex variables. Partial results are known: completeness holds for strongly pseudoconvex domains, for bounded pseudoconvex domains with Lipschitz boundary (via the Kobayashi–Fuks metric), and for smooth pseudoconvex domains of finite D'Angelo type (which are Goldilocks/visibility domains). The general smooth pseudoconvex case is still unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Pseudoconvexity, Analytic Discs, and Invariant Metrics (Krantz)
status_evidence.snippet: Boundary behavior of the Kobayashi-Royden metric is studied to address whether bounded smooth pseudoconvex domains are Kobayashi complete.
status_evidence.claim: The completeness question for the Kobayashi metric on bounded smooth pseudoconvex domains is treated as an open motivating problem.

status_evidence.title: Propagation of regularity for Monge-Ampère exhaustions and Kobayashi metrics
status_evidence.snippet: Partial regularity and completeness results are established under additional assumptions such as existence of smooth Monge-Ampère exhaustions.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial results toward Kobayashi completeness are available in the smooth pseudoconvex setting.

status_evidence.title: Notions of visibility with respect to the Kobayashi distance
status_evidence.snippet: Smooth pseudoconvex domains of finite D'Angelo type are Goldilocks, hence Kobayashi complete.
status_evidence.claim: Completeness is known in the finite-type subclass, but not in full generality.
